title: Model Catalog: Model Selection & Verified Profiles — Messaging Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook drafts positioning and tactical messaging for the Model Catalog surface: how we present open models, our ‘verified profiles’ (performance + quality summaries), and the narrative developers and platform teams need to pick a model for production. It is intentionally practical — copy, console microcopy, objections and rebuttals, and launch mechanics.

Audience and use cases to shape messaging:
- Startup product engineer: needs fast iteration, predictable latency, and predictable costs. Cares about getting to a prototype and then scaling without surprises.
- Mid-market/Enterprise ML platform lead: needs governance, reproducibility, and SLAs; they will care about verifiable metrics and an audit trail.
- Solutions Engineer / PoC owner: needs clear comparators to recommend a model for customers, and quick test harnesses to validate with customer prompts.

Core narrative pillars (short):
1) Trust through reproducible, compact signals — Verified Profiles summarize what actually matters (latency, cost/token, quality on task families, tokenization quirks, known failure modes).
2) Developer-first discovery — find the best fit quickly: search by task, cost bucket, latency SLO, and example prompts.
3) Economical production — we recommend quantization and batching options per profile to reduce costs without surprise regressions.
4) Safe fallbacks — routing and fallback recommendations when capacity or quality gaps appear.

Elevator pitch options (one-liners):
- For engineers: "Pick a model you can trust. Our Verified Profiles show how models actually perform on your workload so you build faster and ship safer."
- For platform teams: "A standardized, auditable catalog of open models — with production-ready performance profiles and rollout recipes."

What a Verified Profile contains (proposed fields):
- Short model summary (architecture, last refresh)
- Typical latency (p50/p95) at standard payload sizes and hardware types
- Cost estimate per 1k tokens under recommended quantization and batch settings
- Task fit scores (generation, summarization, code, chat, instruction-following) — numerical with short text explanation
- Known quirks / failure modes (hallucination on long-context facts; truncated outputs with special tokenization)
- Recommended config (quantization level, KV cache policy, batch size, fallback model)
- Representative example prompts + example outputs (small set to illustrate strengths)
- Benchmark references: internal eval sets + public benchmark links

How we frame open models vs proprietary offerings:
- Honest: open models are vast and fast-moving; quality varies by task and by downstream prompts.
- Value prop: we don’t just catalog models — we run them under consistent conditions and surface practical tradeoffs (cost, latency, quality) so customers can adopt without building their own infra.
- Differentiator vs raw model registries: profiling under production-like settings (batching, KV caching, policy routing) and tying profiles to rollout recipes and monitoring hooks.

Competitive angle and talking points (direct comparisons):
- Open registries (Hugging Face, Model Hubs): "They index models. We profile them end-to-end under production constraints and attach operational recipes."
- LLM API providers (OpenAI, Anthropic): "They provide tight SLAs and curated models. We provide equivalent production guarantees across many model variants plus the ability to run in private or dedicated environments with familiar tooling."
- Inference vendors / runtimes (Replicate, self-hosted runtimes): "They solve serving — we combine serving, catalog, cost-recommendations, and rollout automation so engineering teams don’t re-implement the same evaluation and monitoring plumbing."

Feature-led messaging snippets (for console, docs, marketing):
- Console badge: "Verified profile — production-tested" (hover: "Benchmarked on standard workloads with recommended configs for throughput and cost")
- Search filter label: "Cost bucket" (hover: "Estimated cost per 1k tokens at recommended settings")
- Example tooltip copy: "Fallbacks enabled — auto-route to compatible variant if model is overloaded or out-of-spec"

Model selection workflow (recommended copy for product tour):
1) Discover: "Filter by task, latency SLO, and cost — or paste a prompt to find models that historically perform well on similar prompts."
2) Validate: "Run your prompt set in our sandbox (small credit) and compare outputs side-by-side with our sample prompts."
3) Pin & rollout: "Pin a model profile to a route, add a canary with 5% traffic, and enable automatic fallback to a cheaper or more reliable variant."
4) Monitor & iterate: "Quality drift or cost regressions trigger alerts and suggested rollbacks."

Signals we should display prominently in the catalog listing (priority order):
- Task fit score (single-digit summary)
- p95 latency on recommended infra
- Estimated cost per 1k tokens
- Last profiled date (freshness)
- Safety/guardrails notes (sensitive topic risk)

Sample competitive matrix (text form — to be converted to quick visual):
- Criteria: Depth of profiling | Operational recipes | Private deployment support | Cost transparency | Developer UX for discovery
- Redwood: High | High | High | High | High
- Hugging Face: Medium | Low | Medium | Low | Medium
- OpenAI: Low (on arbitrary open models) | Medium (curated) | Low (unless private infra deal) | Medium | High (SDKs)
- Replicate/self-hosted: Low | Low | High | Variable | Low

Handling common buyer objections (FAQ + rebuttals):
- "Open models are low quality/unsafe": "We surface task-fit and failure modes, provide recommended guardrails, and show sample outputs — customers can validate quickly with their prompt sets."
- "How do I know the numbers aren’t synthetic?": "Profiles are produced by running models under reproducible, documented harnesses (config, infra, datasets). We publish refresh dates and raw benchmark outputs for audit."
- "We already benchmark internally": "Great — import your prompt suites and compare apples-to-apples with our profiles; you can pin the model that wins your tests and keep it under our rollout and monitoring tooling."

Product copy drafts (short):
- Listing snippet: "ModelX — Strong for instruction and chat; low cost at 8-bit quantization. Verified profile: latency and cost measured on common infra."
- Onboarding CTA: "Run a 10-prompt smoke test — compare 3 models in 2 minutes."

Launch plan snippets and tactical asks for PM/Eng/Research: 
- Research: finalize the verification harness and exportable raw benchmark JSONs per profile (deliverable: harness v1 + API for refresh).
- Eng (Console): display badge + compact signals on listing; in-product prompt-based discovery (search-by-prompt).
- Eng (Serving): link profile recommended configs to deployment templates (autoconfigure quantization, KV cache).
- Marketing: prepare short video demo of "pick a model, run your prompt, pin and rollout" and one-pager for sales.
- Sales/SE: script + objection playbook and a small hands-on lab for customers to validate.

KPIs to measure success (first 90 days post-launch):
- % of new Hosted routes that use a Verified Profile at creation (target 45%)
- Average time from discovery -> pinned model (target under 15 minutes for dev persona)
- Reduction in post-deployment incidents attributed to model mismatch (target 20% fewer incidents)
- Number of imported customer prompt suites used for validation (target 30 customers)

Open questions & decisions needed:
- Absolute vs relative scoring for Task Fit — do we present raw scores or normalized comparisons per task family? (risk: raw scores are misunderstood)
- Granularity of performance reporting: one profile per model-version or per model-variant+quantization combo? (cost vs clarity tradeoff)
- Public transparency: what raw data do we publish vs keep internal for customers only?

Next steps (immediate):
- Sync with Research on benchmark harness API and schema (owner: Asha) — due: 2025-11-24
- Design quick mocks for profile card and prompt-based search (owner: Marta) — due: 2025-11-28
- Draft SE one-pager and lab script (owner: Jonah) — due: 2025-12-02

Notes to self / informal brainstorm:
- Could gamify model discovery: "try this challenge prompt and see which model passes" — useful for dev adoption.
- Consider a small "verified partner" program for model maintainers who want their profiles refreshed weekly (revenue/engagement opportunity).

-- end playbook draft --
